{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Inspect the data
print("First few rows:")
print(df.head())

print("\nData types:")
print(df.dtypes)

print("\nSummary of customer_age:")
print(df['customer_age'].describe())

print("\nValue counts for customer_age:")
print(df['customer_age'].value_counts().sort_index())

print("\nSummary of revenue:")
print(df['revenue'].describe())

print("\nValue counts for revenue:")
print(df['revenue'].value_counts().sort_index())

# Check for the six QA orders with revenue 999999.99
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"\nNumber of QA orders (revenue = 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}")
print(qa_orders[['order_id', 'channel', 'customer_segment', 'customer_age', 'status', 'revenue', 'converted']])

# Replace -1 in customer_age with NaN
df['customer_age'] = df['customer_age'].replace(-1, pd.NA)

# Parse revenue as float after removing commas
# First, ensure revenue is string and remove commas
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
df['revenue'] = pd.to_numeric(df['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Filter out QA orders and refunded orders
# QA orders: revenue == 999999.99
# Refunded orders: status == 'refunded'
valid_orders = df[(df['revenue'] != 999999.99) & (df['status'] == 'completed')]

# Filter for converted customers
converted_customers = valid_orders[valid_orders['converted'] == 1]

# Compute mean age of converted customers
mean_age_converted = converted_customers['customer_age'].mean()

# Output the result
print(f"\nMean age of converted customers: {mean_age_converted}")

# Print evidence
print(f"\nNumber of converted customers: {len(converted_customers)}")
print(f"\nNumber of valid orders (after filtering QA and refunded): {len(valid_orders)}")"}
